lines.trans: She herself asked her brother to play along with her this morning.
It looks like she really did fall seriously in love with you.
Since she is staging such foolishness for your sake.
Nikita, tell me quickly, where is your father right now?
It seems to me he went to his restaurant recently.

Everything is fine, and is your ex not bothering you?
He sure is bothering me, he calls me constantly.

Of course he will, after all a brother always worries!
Alright, I will go, what if another brother shows up.
And thinks that I am hitting on you again!

examples.text: Представляешь, за меня ещё никогда никто не дрался!
examples.trans: Can you imagine, nobody has ever fought over me before!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Денис, расскажи, как у тебя со Светой?
examples.trans: Denis, tell me, how are things with you and Sveta?

examples.text: Никак, это было просто чтобы Катя поревновала.
examples.trans: Nothing at all, that was just to make Katya jealous.

examples.text: Видел я вчера, как у вас после текилы было.
examples.trans: I saw yesterday how it was with you two after tequila.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоянно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ещё как надоедает, он мне постоянно звонит.
examples.trans: He sure is bothering me, he calls me constantly.

examples.text: Что ты постоянно боишься?
examples.trans: What are you constantly afraid of?

examples.text: Он постоянно опаздывал на работу.
examples.trans: He was constantly late for work.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is calling', paired with 'позвонить'.

examples.text: Всё, Миша, пока, не звони мне больше.
examples.trans: That is it, Misha, bye, do not call me anymore.

examples.text: Если бы ты брал трубку, когда звонит брат.
examples.trans: If you picked up the phone when your brother calls.

examples.text: Так давай прямо сейчас позвоним в эту компанию.
examples.trans: Then let us call that company right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера я пришла домой и не смогла врать.
examples.trans: Yesterday I came home and could not lie to him.

examples.text: У меня живот заболел, и я домой пошла.
examples.trans: My stomach hurt, and I went home.

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Ладно, мне пора идти и работать с продуктами.
examples.trans: Alright, it is time for me to go and work with the groceries.

examples.text: Поэтому извините меня, пожалуйста, мне надо идти работать.
examples.trans: So excuse me, please, I have to go work.

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am afraid'.

examples.text: Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Я не боюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

examples.text: Ладно, я пойду, вдруг ещё один брат появится.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go, what if another brother shows up.

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся?
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait in ambush'.

related.gloss: to to wait in ambush (prefixed perfective)
not to to wait in ambush (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и караулить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to wait in ambush on time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Может быть, проще ей всё подробно объяснить?
examples.trans: Maybe it is simpler to explain everything to her in detail?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно понимаю, если что, я в своём номере.
examples.trans: Of course I understand, if anything comes up, I am in my room.

examples.text: Вы, конечно же, слышали об устричных фермах?
examples.trans: You have, of course, heard about oyster farms?

examples.text: Конечно, ведь вы же господин Баринов Валентин?
examples.trans: Of course, after all you are Mr. Barinov Valentin, right?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, ведь мне он ничего не рассказывает.
examples.trans: That is good, because he tells me nothing at all.

examples.text: Просто она ведёт себя так, будто мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: She just acts as if we are dating.

examples.text: Ей сейчас тяжело, ведь она с парнем рассталась.
examples.trans: It is hard for her right now, because she broke up with her boyfriend.

meanings.en: dear, darling, my friend (in address: родной мой)
meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own, native').

examples.text: Парни, вы чего, ведь Света родная сестра моя!
examples.trans: Guys, what is with you, Sveta is my own sister!

examples.text: Подожди, как это она твоя родная сестра?
examples.trans: Wait, how is she your own sister?

examples.text: Парни, ведь Света моя родная сестра!
examples.trans: Guys, Sveta is my own sister!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.text: Конечно будет, ведь родной брат всегда волнуется!
examples.trans: Of course he will, after all a brother always worries!

examples.text: Все-таки родной брат всегда волнуется!
examples.trans: After all, a brother always worries!

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, родным людям всегда нужно доверять!
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, you always need to trust your own people!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

examples.text: Не волнуйся.
examples.trans: Don't worry.

examples.text: Я волнуюсь.
examples.trans: I'm nervous.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, не буду.
examples.trans: Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, пойдём скорее ко мне в кабинет.
examples.trans: Alright, let us go quickly to my office.

examples.text: Ладно, жду, только на кухне зови меня Виктор Петрович.
examples.trans: Alright, I am waiting, just call me Viktor Petrovich in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ладно, мне пора идти и работать с продуктами.
examples.trans: Alright, it is time for me to go and work with the groceries.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Ладно, пойдём скорее ко мне в кабинет.
examples.trans: Alright, let us go quickly to my office.

examples.text: Я просто первую машину на улице поймал.
examples.trans: I just flagged down the first car on the street.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее отсюда внутрь отеля.
examples.trans: Let us go inside the hotel from here quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы будем разводить свежих устриц здесь, в России.
examples.trans: We will raise fresh oysters here in Russia.

examples.text: Валя, ты повторяешься, устриц ты уже разводил.
examples.trans: Valya, you are repeating yourself, you already raised oysters.

examples.text: Где же мы теперь этого водителя найдём?
examples.trans: Where will we find that driver now?

meanings.en: to appear, to show up, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'явиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'shows up, appears', paired with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!

examples.text: У нас появилась хорошая идея.
examples.trans: We came up with a good idea.

examples.text: Я тебе серьёзно говорю. Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously. Let him just show up here one more time!

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (it over)', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: И подумает, что я снова к тебе пристаю!
examples.trans: And thinks that I am hitting on you again!

examples.text: Я даже подумать не мог, что всё так серьёзно.
examples.trans: I could not even imagine that everything was so serious.

examples.text: Я подумаю.
examples.trans: I'll think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никак, это было просто чтобы Катя поревновала.
examples.trans: Nothing at all, that was just to make Katya jealous.

examples.text: Слушай, а Света знает, что у вас ничего нет?
examples.trans: Listen, does Sveta know that there is nothing between you two?

examples.text: Потому что он уже давно сидит здесь.
examples.trans: Because he has been sitting here for a long time already.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: И подумает, что я снова к тебе пристаю!
examples.trans: And thinks that I am hitting on you again!

examples.text: Мне кажется, я прекрасно понимаю, про кого вы говорите.
examples.trans: It seems to me I understand perfectly whom you are talking about.

examples.text: Он снова здесь.
examples.trans: He's here again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там сейчас свежее мясо должны привезти, проконтролируй.
examples.trans: They are supposed to deliver fresh meat there right now, go check it.

examples.text: Сеня, вчера вечеринка у тебя получилась отличная.
examples.trans: Senya, your party yesterday turned out great.

examples.text: Денис, расскажи, как у тебя со Светой?
examples.trans: Denis, tell me, how are things with you and Sveta?

meanings.en: to pester, to bother, to harass (+ к + dat.)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ставать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to pester, to harass', paired with 'пристать'.

examples.text: Они приставали к Нине.
examples.trans: They were pestering Nina.

examples.text: Не приставай ко мне с вопросами!
examples.trans: Stop pestering me with questions!

examples.text: Они приставали к Нине. Нина, ну расскажите вы ему!
examples.trans: They were pestering Nina. Nina, come on, tell him!

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.text: Он всё-таки пришёл.
examples.trans: He came after all.

examples.text: Может, всё-таки пойдём?
examples.trans: Maybe we'll go after all?

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?
